texts: mixed: the rule fires and covers the whole sentence, but the nightmoths are recorded as prey the hunt physically changes rather than as the unchanged quarry, which asserts a change to the moths the sentence never states (the adjudicator confirmed it). That is a translator-side role slip, not a wording fault — the same verb was handled correctly in your third text — so no rewrite is called for here; the phrasing is already the shape that parses best, one finite clause per condition with an explicit subject.

Again a translator-side slip rather than a phrasing fault: your near-identical third text, "the nightmoth crowd at that lantern-row thins", was parsed correctly, so this sentence needs no rewrite.
